 Order
(Dated this the 19th day of December, 2025)

The petitioner is the sole accused in S.C No.527 of 2018
pending before the Special Court for Sc and St (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, arising out of Crime
No.2933 of 2017 of Angamaly Police Station, Ernakulam
. The offences alleged against the petitioner is under Sections 376(2)(n), 313 and 506 of IPC and Sections 3(1)(w), 3(2)(v)(a) of SC and ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Act.

entities.text: SC and ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Act
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: 2. The prosecution case is that, when the de facto complainant was working as a home nurse in the residence of the petitioner, during the period from October 2016 to October 2017, after promising to marry her, he sexually abused her and thereby he is alleged to have committed the aforesaid offences.

3. According to the learned counsel for the petitioner, the entire dispute between the petitioner and the de facto complainant were settled and therefore, he prayed for quashing all further proceedings against the petitioner.
4. The de facto complainant also filed an affidavit stating that the matter has been settled and she prayed for quashing all further proceedings against the petitioner.
4. The petition was opposed by the learned Public 2025:KER:98411 Prosecutor.

5. On a perusal of the FI statement, it can be seen that the de facto complainant was already married to another person and the said marriage was not dissolved when she started relationship with the petitioner.
The relationship between the petitioner and the de facto complainant continued for more than one year.
Therefore, the claim in the FI statement that she had given consent to the relationship with the petitioner due to promise of marriage cannot be believed.
So, the relationship between them was a consensual one.

It is also revealed from the affidavit filed by the de facto complainant in support of the Crl.M.C.
6.
In the above circumstances, no useful purpose will be served in continuing the proceedings against the petitioner, as it will only be an abuse of the process of law.
Therefore, this Crl. M.C is allowed.

All further proceedings against the petitioner in S.C No.527 of 2018 pending before the Special Court for SC and ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, arising out of Crime No.2933 of 2017 of Angamaly Police Station, Ernakulam, stands quashed under Section 528 of B.N.S.S. Sd/-
C.
